title: Aquatic surface entries on OCEAN2, an ocean embark that is actually WET: 58% surface water, water on all four map edges, and the ocean tile 3,28 present in plotinfo.border. Same design as E14-OCEAN — open every aquatic surface entry on the site and neighbour tiles at 50, close every land entry, release surface holds every 1,500 ticks, 20,000 ticks — plus a natural arm. Does a wet ocean map produce shark and fish waves?
fork: F14 follow-up 2: E14-OCEAN had NO surface water and never debited a shark entry; E14-LAKE was 87% water and drew hippos, milkfish and an otter. OCEAN2 separates 'no edge water' from 'the ocean tile is not in the border list'.

predictions.expects: arm aquatic: shark/fish/ray waves from the ocean tiles, entries debited by exactly the arrivals, as milkfish did on LAKE

predictions.model: ocean entries never wave, whatever the map
predictions.expects: arm aquatic: no shark or fish arrival and no debit in 2 x 20,000 ticks while the natural arm produces waves
arm aquatic: crabs and saltwater crocodiles only, no AQUATIC+IMMOBILE_LAND species

kill_criterion: any arrival of an AQUATIC+IMMOBILE_LAND species (shark, fish, ray, whale) settles it; a debit with no arrival is the second instrument; the natural arm must produce waves or the fort is not comparable
culling: drop a replicate on any breach or changed save

pre: local site=df.world_site.find(df.global.plotinfo.site_id); local x0,x1=math.floor(site.global_min_x/16),math.floor(site.global_max_x/16); local y0,y1=math.floor(site.global_min_y/16),math.floor(site.global_max_y/16); local o,c,names=0,0,{}; for _,p in ipairs(df.global.world.populations.all) do local r=p.population; if p.type==df.world_population_type.Animal and r.feature_idx<0 and r.cave_id<0 and r.region_x>=x0-1 and r.region_x<=x1+1 and r.region_y>=y0-1 and r.region_y<=y1+1 and p.quantity_max<10000000 then local cr=df.creature_raw.find(p.race); local id=cr and cr.creature_id or ''; local aq = id:match('^FISH_') or id:match('^SHARK_') or id:match('WHALE') or id=='ORCA' or id:match('OTTER') or id:match('CROCODILE') or id=='ALLIGATOR' or id:match('HIPPO') or id:match('PLATYPUS') or id:match('TURTLE') or id=='BEAVER' or id:match('^SEAL') or id=='CRAB' or id:match('DOLPHIN') or id:match('MANATEE') or id:match('WALRUS'); if aq then p.quantity=50; p.flags.extinct=false; o=o+1; names[id]=true else p.quantity=0; p.flags.extinct=true; c=c+1 end end end; local l={}; for k in pairs(names) do l[#l+1]=k end; table.sort(l); print(('aquatic opened: %d entries (%s); closed: %d'):format(o, table.concat(l,' '), c))
